tasks.title: Add sectioned `properties` export to arc-letterbox.js
tasks.description: Append an `export const properties = { sections: [...] }` block to the bottom of `apps/scene-engine/public/modules/components/arc-letterbox/arc-letterbox.js` (after the existing default-export render function). The schema must cover every key the renderer reads in lines 30–39 (`top-height`, `bottom-height`, `top-curve`, `bottom-curve`, `contour`, `color`, `opacity`, `edge-feather`) — no more, no less. Group into four sections: (1) `top-bar` / `Top Bar` → `top-height`, `top-curve`; (2) `bottom-bar` / `Bottom Bar` → `bottom-height`, `bottom-curve`; (3) `curvature` / `Curvature` → `contour`; (4) `appearance` / `Appearance` → `color`, `opacity`, `edge-feather`. Use `type: 'number'` for every numeric property with `min`/`max`/`step` matching the existing renderer clamp ranges (e.g. `top-height` is `pct(..., 0, 50)` so `min: 0, max: 50, step: 0.5`; `bottom-curve` is `pct(..., 50, 100)` so `min: 50, max: 100, step: 0.5`; `contour` is `pct(..., 0, 50)` so `min: 0, max: 50, step: 0.5`; `opacity` is `clamp(..., 0, 1)` so `min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01`; `edge-feather` is `pct(..., 0, 8)` so `min: 0, max: 8, step: 0.1`). Use `type: 'string'` for `color`. Each property gets a Title-Case `label` and a sentence-case `description` (1–2 sentences, editor-facing, no implementation jargon — match the voice in `press-start.js` / `procedural-sphere.js`). Each section may carry its own short `description` summarizing the group. Add a single-line comment `// Inspector schema for editor use only — runtime ignores it.` immediately above the `export const properties = ...` line, matching the comment in `press-start.js`. Do NOT modify the render function, the `DEFAULTS` constant, or any other code in the file. Do NOT add `default` fields to any PropertyDef (per session decision: defaults stay as render-time fallbacks).

Group into 11 sections in this order: (1) `animation` / `Animation` → `animate`; (2) `position` / `Position` → `center-x`, `center-y`; (3) `geometry` / `Geometry` → `radius`, `inner-radius`, `outer-radius`, `depth-curve`, `radius-x`; (4) `strips` / `Strips` → `strip-count`, `strip-width`, `curve-steps`, `rotation-offset`, `minimum-open`; (5) `appearance` / `Appearance` → `opacity`, `composite`; (6) `gate-timing` / `Gate Timing` → `closed-hold-seconds`, `transition-seconds`, `open-hold-seconds`, `gate-offset-seconds`; (7) `palette` / `Palette` → `palette-mode`, `color-cycle`, `color-offset`, `color-speed`, `color-bias`; (8) `melee-spectrum` / `Melee Spectrum Colors` → `color-start`, `color-mid`, `color-end`, `color-magenta`; (9) `hue-wheel` / `Hue Wheel Colors` → `wheel-hue-shift`, `wheel-saturation`, `wheel-lightness`, `wheel-mint-lift`, `wheel-softness`, `wheel-contrast`; (10) `texture` / `Texture` → `texture-angle`, `texture-speed`, `texture-scale`, `texture-resolution`; (11) `performance` / `Performance` → `target-fps`, `dpr-cap`. For `radius-x` (the legacy fallback for `radius` on line 337), append ` (legacy)` to the label and start the description with `Legacy fallback for \`radius\`. `. Use `type: 'number'` for all numeric properties with `min`/`max`/`step` matching the renderer's clamp ranges (e.g. `inner-radius` is `clamp(..., 0, 1)` so `min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01`; `outer-radius` is `clamp(..., 0.05, 3)` so `min: 0.05, max: 3, step: 0.01`; `depth-curve` is `clamp(..., 0.2, 4)` so `min: 0.2, max: 4, step: 0.01`; `strip-count` is `Math.max(4, Math.round(...))` so `min: 4, step: 1`; `strip-width` is `clamp(..., 0.05, 1.5)` so `min: 0.05, max: 1.5, step: 0.01`; `curve-steps` is `Math.max(3, Math.round(...))` so `min: 3, step: 1`; `opacity` is `clamp(..., 0, 1)` so `min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01`; `minimum-open` is `clamp(..., 0, 1)` so `min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01`; `closed-hold-seconds` / `open-hold-seconds` are `clamp(..., 0, 10)` so `min: 0, max: 10, step: 0.01`; `transition-seconds` is `clamp(..., 0.02, 10)` so `min: 0.02, max: 10, step: 0.01`; `wheel-saturation` is `clamp(..., 0, 1.2)` so `min: 0, max: 1.2, step: 0.01`; `wheel-lightness` is `clamp(..., 0.08, 0.86)` so `min: 0.08, max: 0.86, step: 0.01`; `wheel-mint-lift` is `clamp(..., -0.2, 0.35)` so `min: -0.2, max: 0.35, step: 0.01`; `wheel-softness` is `clamp(..., 0, 1)` so `min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01`; `wheel-contrast` is `clamp(..., 0, 1.5)` so `min: 0, max: 1.5, step: 0.01`; `texture-scale` is `clamp(..., 0.2, 4)` so `min: 0.2, max: 4, step: 0.01`; `texture-resolution` is `clamp(..., 0.2, 1)` so `min: 0.2, max: 1, step: 0.01`; `target-fps` is `clamp(..., 1, 60)` so `min: 1, max: 60, step: 1`; `dpr-cap` is `clamp(..., 1, 2)` so `min: 1, max: 2, step: 0.1`; `rotation-offset` and `texture-angle` are degree values with no clamp so `step: 1`; `wheel-hue-shift` is also a degree value so `min: 0, max: 360, step: 1`). Use `type: 'boolean'` for `animate`. Use `type: 'select'` for `palette-mode` with options `['melee-spectrum', 'hue-wheel', 'tri-color']`. Use `type: 'string'` for `color-start`, `color-mid`, `color-end`, `color-magenta`, and `composite`. Each property gets a Title-Case `label` and a sentence-case `description` (1–2 sentences, editor-facing, v1 voice). Each section gets its own short `description` summarizing the group. Add the single-line comment `// Inspector schema for editor use only — runtime ignores it.` immediately above the `export const properties = ...` line. Do NOT modify the render function, helpers, or any other code in the file. Do NOT add `default` fields to any PropertyDef.

NO `properties` export — falls back to General orphan render in the inspector.

Legacy key `radius-x` carries a ' (legacy)' label suffix. No changes to helpers or the render function.

actions.command: APPEND BLANK LINE AFTER default export (line 490) IN apps/scene-engine/public/modules/components/procedural-cylinder-strips/procedural-cylinder-strips-mask.js

ADD section-level description FOR section `animation` SUMMARIZING that this toggle freezes or runs the gate-open animation and the color/texture phase scrolling.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `animate` (type=boolean, label='Animate', description='Whether the gate-open animation and palette/texture phase scrolling advance over time. Disable to render a still frame at t=0.') UNDER section `animation`
ADD section-level description FOR section `position` SUMMARIZING that these are the normalized 0–1 coordinates of the tunnel center within the layer; 0.5,0.5 is dead center.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `center-x` (type=number, label='Center X', description='Horizontal position of the tunnel center, expressed as a fraction of layer width. 0 is the left edge, 1 is the right edge.', min=0, max=1, step=0.01) UNDER section `position`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `center-y` (type=number, label='Center Y', description='Vertical position of the tunnel center, expressed as a fraction of layer height. 0 is the top edge, 1 is the bottom edge.', min=0, max=1, step=0.01) UNDER section `position`

ADD section-level description FOR section `geometry` SUMMARIZING that these knobs shape the tunnel itself — overall scale, the inner ring radius, the outer ring radius, and how the depth between them is eased.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `radius` (type=number, label='Radius', description='Overall tunnel radius as a fraction of layer width and height. Values above 1 push the outer ring beyond the layer edges.', min=0, step=0.01) UNDER section `geometry`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `inner-radius` (type=number, label='Inner Radius', description='Where each strip starts at the back of the tunnel, as a fraction of `radius`. 0 collapses the strips to a point at the center.', min=0, max=1, step=0.01) UNDER section `geometry`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `outer-radius` (type=number, label='Outer Radius', description='Where each strip ends at the front of the tunnel, as a fraction of `radius`. Values above 1 extend the strips past the nominal radius.', min=0.05, max=3, step=0.01) UNDER section `geometry`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `depth-curve` (type=number, label='Depth Curve', description='Easing exponent applied between inner and outer radius. 1 is linear; higher values bunch strips toward the front, lower values bunch them toward the back.', min=0.2, max=4, step=0.01) UNDER section `geometry`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `radius-x` (type=number, label='Radius X (legacy)', description='Legacy fallback for `radius`. Older scenes set this key to size the tunnel; new scenes should use `radius`.', min=0, step=0.01) UNDER section `geometry`
ADD section-level description FOR section `strips` SUMMARIZING that these knobs control how many radial slats divide the tunnel, how wide each slat is, and how its curve is tessellated.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `strip-count` (type=number, label='Strip Count', description='Number of radial slats around the tunnel. Higher values produce a finer grille at the cost of fill rate.', min=4, step=1) UNDER section `strips`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `strip-width` (type=number, label='Strip Width', description='Fraction of each strip slot occupied by the slat itself. 1 fills the slot edge-to-edge; lower values leave gaps between adjacent slats even when fully open.', min=0.05, max=1.5, step=0.01) UNDER section `strips`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `curve-steps` (type=number, label='Curve Steps', description='Number of line segments used to tessellate each slat from inner to outer radius. Higher values produce smoother curves; lower values produce a faceted look.', min=3, step=1) UNDER section `strips`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `rotation-offset` (type=number, label='Rotation Offset', description='Static rotation applied to the entire strip ring, in degrees. Use to align the gap between strips with other on-stage elements.', min=0, max=360, step=1) UNDER section `strips`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `minimum-open` (type=number, label='Minimum Open', description='Floor on the gate-open amount, 0–1. 0 lets the strips fully close; higher values keep them at least this far open even at the bottom of the cycle.', min=0, max=1, step=0.01) UNDER section `strips`
ADD section-level description FOR section `appearance` SUMMARIZING that opacity dims the textured strips uniformly and composite controls how the strips blend onto the canvas underneath.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `opacity` (type=number, label='Opacity', description='Overall opacity of the strip mask, 0–1. Applied uniformly after the texture is masked through the strips.', min=0, max=1, step=0.01) UNDER section `appearance`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `composite` (type=string, label='Composite Mode', description='Canvas global composite operation used when drawing the masked texture (e.g. `source-over`, `screen`, `lighter`). Defaults to `source-over`.') UNDER section `appearance`

ADD section-level description FOR section `gate-timing` SUMMARIZING that the strips animate as a four-phase gate — closed hold, opening transition, open hold, closing transition — and these knobs set the duration of each phase plus a phase offset.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `closed-hold-seconds` (type=number, label='Closed Hold', description='Seconds spent fully closed at the bottom of the gate cycle before opening.', min=0, max=10, step=0.01) UNDER section `gate-timing`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `transition-seconds` (type=number, label='Transition', description='Seconds spent ramping between closed and open. Used for both the opening and closing transitions.', min=0.02, max=10, step=0.01) UNDER section `gate-timing`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `open-hold-seconds` (type=number, label='Open Hold', description='Seconds spent fully open at the top of the gate cycle before closing.', min=0, max=10, step=0.01) UNDER section `gate-timing`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `gate-offset-seconds` (type=number, label='Gate Offset', description='Phase offset added to the gate clock, in seconds. Use to desynchronize multiple strip layers so they open at different times.', step=0.01) UNDER section `gate-timing`

ADD section-level description FOR section `palette` SUMMARIZING that these knobs choose the palette mode and shape how the chosen palette is sampled across the texture — how many cycles fit, where it starts, how fast it scrolls, and how the gradient is biased.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `palette-mode` (type=select, label='Palette Mode', description='Which color algorithm fills the texture. `melee-spectrum` is the canonical Melee gradient, `hue-wheel` walks the full HSL hue circle, and `tri-color` interpolates the three custom colors below.', options=['melee-spectrum', 'hue-wheel', 'tri-color']) UNDER section `palette`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-cycle` (type=number, label='Color Cycle', description='How many full palette cycles span one texture sweep. Higher values pack more bands into the same area.', step=0.01) UNDER section `palette`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-offset` (type=number, label='Color Offset', description='Static phase offset applied to the palette sample position, 0–1 wraps. Use to dial in which color sits at the front of the texture at t=0.', step=0.01) UNDER section `palette`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-speed` (type=number, label='Color Speed', description='Rate at which the palette scrolls through the texture per second. 0 freezes the palette in place; negative values reverse the scroll.', step=0.01) UNDER section `palette`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-bias` (type=number, label='Color Bias', description='Exponent applied to the palette sample position before lookup. 1 is linear; higher values bias toward the start of the palette, lower values bias toward the end.', min=0.1, step=0.01) UNDER section `palette`

ADD section-level description FOR section `melee-spectrum` SUMMARIZING that these four colors define the canonical Melee gradient stops; they feed `melee-spectrum` mode directly and `tri-color` mode minus the magenta.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-start` (type=string, label='Start Color', description='First gradient stop. The blue end of the canonical Melee spectrum. Hex string (e.g. `#2030ff`).') UNDER section `melee-spectrum`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-mid` (type=string, label='Mid Color', description='Middle gradient stop. The violet bridge between blue and red. Hex string (e.g. `#3f2dff`).') UNDER section `melee-spectrum`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-end` (type=string, label='End Color', description='Last gradient stop. The red/pink end of the canonical Melee spectrum. Hex string (e.g. `#ff2f75`).') UNDER section `melee-spectrum`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `color-magenta` (type=string, label='Magenta Accent', description='Optional magenta accent woven between the violet and red stops in `melee-spectrum` mode. Hex string (e.g. `#ac2ba0`); falls back to a midpoint of mid+end when unset.') UNDER section `melee-spectrum`

ADD section-level description FOR section `hue-wheel` SUMMARIZING that these knobs only apply when palette mode is `hue-wheel` — they shape how the HSL hue circle is sampled, weighted, and contrast-adjusted before being painted across the texture.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `wheel-hue-shift` (type=number, label='Hue Shift', description='Starting hue of the wheel, in degrees. Rotates the entire palette around the HSL hue circle.', min=0, max=360, step=1) UNDER section `hue-wheel`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `wheel-saturation` (type=number, label='Saturation', description='Base saturation applied to every hue, 0–1.2. The renderer can pull saturation lower in the mint band; it never pushes it higher than this floor.', min=0, max=1.2, step=0.01) UNDER section `hue-wheel`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `wheel-lightness` (type=number, label='Lightness', description='Base lightness applied to every hue. Per-band lifts and dips are added on top of this baseline.', min=0.08, max=0.86, step=0.01) UNDER section `hue-wheel`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `wheel-mint-lift` (type=number, label='Mint Lift', description='Extra lightness added to the green/mint band. Positive values brighten greens; negative values push them into shadow.', min=-0.2, max=0.35, step=0.01) UNDER section `hue-wheel`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `wheel-softness` (type=number, label='Softness', description='How wide the per-hue band weighting falls off. Higher values blur the bands together for a smoother wheel; lower values keep each band tight.', min=0, max=1, step=0.01) UNDER section `hue-wheel`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `wheel-contrast` (type=number, label='Contrast', description='Final RGB contrast multiplier applied around the 128 midpoint. 1 leaves colors untouched; values below 1 wash them out; values above 1 deepen them.', min=0, max=1.5, step=0.01) UNDER section `hue-wheel`

ADD section-level description FOR section `texture` SUMMARIZING that the palette is painted onto an offscreen texture which is then masked by the strips; these knobs orient that texture, scroll it over time, and trade resolution for performance.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `texture-angle` (type=number, label='Texture Angle', description='Rotation of the gradient bands across the texture, in degrees. 0 runs the bands horizontally; 90 runs them vertically.', min=-180, max=180, step=1) UNDER section `texture`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `texture-speed` (type=number, label='Texture Speed', description='Additional scroll rate added to the palette phase per second. Stacks on top of `color-speed`.', step=0.01) UNDER section `texture`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `texture-scale` (type=number, label='Texture Scale', description='Multiplier on band density and gradient extent. Higher values pack more bands into the same texture; the band count adapts automatically for hue-wheel and melee-spectrum modes.', min=0.2, max=4, step=0.01) UNDER section `texture`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `texture-resolution` (type=number, label='Texture Resolution', description='Offscreen texture resolution as a fraction of layer size, 0.2–1. Lower values are cheaper to redraw; 1 matches the layer pixel-for-pixel.', min=0.2, max=1, step=0.01) UNDER section `texture`
ADD section-level description FOR section `performance` SUMMARIZING that these caps trade visual fidelity for cost — they bound the redraw rate and the pixel ratio used when sizing the canvas.

ADD PropertyDef FOR `target-fps` (type=number, label='Target FPS', description='Maximum redraw rate, capped at 60. Lower values reduce GPU/CPU load at the cost of choppier motion.', min=1, max=60, step=1) UNDER section `performance`

ADD PropertyDef FOR `dpr-cap` (type=number, label='DPR Cap', description='Upper bound on the device pixel ratio used when sizing the canvas. 1 forces logical-pixel rendering; 2 allows up to retina sharpness.', min=1, max=2, step=0.1) UNDER section `performance`
